transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Anita Rao (Lakeside), Marcus Lee (Lakeside), Sophie Turner (Lakeside)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and cost breakdown. Customer curious about route-level cost attribution, tagging production vs experiments, and Dedicated vs Hosted economics for 24/7 triage models. Security questions around SSO, SOC2, and KMS noted. Agreed next steps: pricing, security pack, traffic profile + pilot.

Topics:
- Per-route dashboards and tagging
- Cost breakdown by model + route
- Alerts and SLOs per route
- Autoscaling / dedicated capacity questions
- Security (SOC2, SSO, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: All right hi everyone uh thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, um I think we have about 45 minutes, I see Anita, Marcus, Sophie - thanks for making time. Liam from our infra team will run through the console.
[00:12] Anita: Hey hey, yeah excited, we just want to see the per-route cost stuff - we've got a mix of triage models and longer generative pipelines so cost attribution is a big ask.
[00:20] Liam: Cool, I'll share my screen - let me know if the deck link doesn't load. (link shared: https://redwood.app/decks/console-walkthrough)
[00:35] Maya: Quick intro: Lakeside's main concern is unit economics across routes, and routing to cheaper model variants during off-peak while preserving latency SLOs.
[00:47] Marcus: And we need to be sure audit logs and data residency are covered, we're hitting some regulatory controls for PHI.
[00:55] Liam: Yep understood. We'll cover RBAC, audit logs, and KMS notes near the end - quick caveat the recorded transcript may mislabel some acronyms.
[01:10] Liam: (screen) This is the Console home - top-level usage analytics. You can filter by time range, by model, and importantly by route tag. We recommend tagging at the API gateway: route=triage, route=compose, env=prod/staging.
[01:33] Sophie: When you say "per-route cost" is that token-level breakdown or just request counts?
[01:38] Liam: Great question - we do both. There's per-token cost estimates that map to model variant and quantization profile, and per-request aggregations. The console shows "cost by route" and you can drill down to "cost by model" within that route.
[01:55] Anita: Is the per-token cost exact or an estimate? We have to do chargebacks to internal teams so it needs to be defensible.
[02:02] Liam: It's an estimate derived from unit pricing and profiling. For hosted folks it's near-real-time because we know the idle overhead; for Dedicated you can opt to use measured utilization + allocation rules. We can attach the pricing model - Maya will follow up with a worked example.
[02:20] Marcus: Work example would be great, like show 95th p90 p50 lat and cost per 1k requests.
[02:27] Maya: Yeah we'll prepare a short spreadsheet.
[02:31] Liam: Here is a per-route dashboard - you can see throughput, avg latency, p50/p95, token counts, and an estimated cost bar. You can also set an "allocation percentage" if you want to apportion shared infra across routes.
[02:50] [02:50] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[03:01] Sophie: How does the console handle dynamic batching / KV cache effects? Our seq lengths vary a lot and batching dramatically changes per-token costs.
[03:12] Liam: Good call - we annotate dashboards with "efficiency" metrics: average batch size, cache hit rate (we call it KV cash on the hood sometimes in logs - transcript note, that's KV cache), and you can correlate spikes in batch size to lower unit cost. There's also a model profile tab where we recommend quantization and kernel choices.
[03:38] Anita: Does Redwood recommend turning on prefix caching for triage routes? We worry about stale context.
[03:45] Liam: Typically yes for predictable prompts; we expose TTL and invalidation controls per route. For PHI we recommend not caching or using encrypted cache with customer-managed keys.
[03:59] Marcus: On Dedicated vs Hosted - we need 24/7 for two critical routes and we'd like Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable latency. What's the delta in unit cost?
[04:12] Maya: Generally Dedicated has lower raw per-token infra cost but requires a commit. For low-latency 24/7 traffic Dedicated often wins on TCO. Hosted is better for bursty experimental traffic. We'll send a side-by-side example tailored to your QPS and sequence length.
[04:33] Sophie: And what about fallbacks - if Dedicated pool is saturated can we route to Hosted or smaller models?
[04:39] Liam: Yes - smart routing supports policy-based fallback: region, cost, latency tiers. You can set route rules - e.g., if 95th > 300ms fallback to a cheaper variant, or route to Hosted read replica.
[04:55] Anita: Security - do you have SOC2 and SSO? We need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[05:02] Liam: We are SOC2 Type II. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync, RBAC is fine-grained per-team and per-route. Our audit logs capture token-level usage; we can produce exportable logs for compliance. I'll drop the SOC2 and SSO docs after the call.
[05:22] Maya: Note - KMS options include customer-managed keys in certain Private deployments and partner HSM integrations. Liam will share the KMS integration guide.
[05:32] Marcus: For Private - we may evaluate a VPC deployment for PHI. How different is the Console UX between Hosted and Private?
[05:40] Liam: UX is the same; control plane is similar but in Private the data plane is customer-managed. We maintain the same dashboards and remote telemetry with opt-in. There are some differences in retention windows but functionally the Console mirrors Hosted.
[05:58] Maya: Demoing a couple of drilldowns - here's route "triage-icu": you can click into the route and see per-model token distribution, egress cost, and contributor teams.
[06:18] Liam: Also you can tag requests with metadata (customer_id, feature_flag) and later pivot on that to see how much a given feature costs.
[06:28] Sophie: Can we export per-route billable reports to our finance system? CSV/JSON?
[06:32] Liam: Yep exports are CSV/JSON and we also have a reporting API for programmatic pulls.
[06:39] Anita: Any built-in anomaly detection for cost regressions? We had a silent perf regression before and it spiked spend.
[06:46] Liam: Yes - "Cost Regression Alerts" can be tied to a baseline and thresholds; alerts can go to Slack, PagerDuty, or email. We also tie regressions to recent model rollouts so you can quickly narrow root cause.
[07:00] [07:00] Speaker 2: (brief noise)
[07:12] Marcus: About model rollouts - does the Console show traffic split and can we do canary / A/B?
[07:18] Liam: Exactly - there's a rollout tab per model where you can configure canary percentages, duration, and automatic rollback rules if latency or quality metrics degrade.
[07:30] Anita: Speaking of quality metrics, do you integrate evals or do we need to ship our own?
[07:36] Liam: You can upload prompt sets and eval results; we also integrate with open eval frameworks. We surface quality regressions alongside cost regressions.
[07:50] Sophie: For our accounting team we need attribution to business unit - is that done with tags?
[07:56] Maya: Yes tagging + allocation rules. You can set allocation rules based on request tag and percent split; that flows into the cost report.
[08:09] Marcus: Can you demo a sample cost breakdown?
[08:13] Liam: Sure - opening a sample report. (pauses) Here you can see route-level cost for last 30 days: triage-icu: 42% of spend, compose-notes: 28%, experiments: 12%, infra & overhead: 18%. We break infra & overhead into GPU idle, memory, and storage.
[08:34] Anita: How is idle GPU cost attributed?
[08:37] Liam: We have configurable allocation rules - either allocate proportionally by active token count or by a fixed baseline per route.
[08:45] Sophie: Is there a feature to show hypothetical savings if we quantize a model from fp16 to int8?
[08:51] Liam: Yep - the Optimize suggestions tab will give projected savings and expected latency impact for quantization and batch tuning. It's a recommendation engine - you can export a set of suggested changes.
[09:05] Anita: We also have a regulatory question - retention of logs with PHI. Can we set retention policies per environment?
[09:12] Liam: Yes, retention windows are configurable per tenant and per route; for Private deployments you can set local retention and disabled telemetry.
[09:21] Marcus: If we do a pilot, can we run a perf benchmark with our traffic and see actual cost numbers?
[09:26] Maya: Absolutely - common pilot is 1-week with shadowing. We'll run a benchmark harness and produce a burn report.
[09:33] Sophie: What's the SLA on Dedicated? We need 99.9 for latency-critical routes.
[09:38] Maya: Dedicated SLA is 99.9 availability for the pool; we have latency SLO guidance you can set per-route. We'll share the SLA doc.
[09:46] Anita: A couple nitty gritty items - we have auto-scaling constraints, we need to know burst-to-burst cold start behavior.
[09:53] Liam: The runtime supports continuous batching and cold-start mitigation. Cold starts are usually bounded by model warmup time; we recommend pre-warming for critical routes.
[10:05] [10:05] Speaker 3: (coffee sip)
[10:18] Marcus: For billing we want invoice-level breakdown by route monthly. Does Redwood support that?
[10:23] Maya: Yes, monthly invoices include per-route breakdown if requested; it's an add-on in the billing settings.
[10:30] Anita: Any limitations on model size for Dedicated? We want to run 50B weights.
[10:36] Liam: We support multi-GPU sharding and kernel selection for large models; 50B is fine depending on cluster config. For very large models we recommend a Dedicated pool.
[10:48] Sophie: Ok last: fallback strategy example again - show me a simple rule.
[10:54] Liam: Example: route triage-icu: prefer model x-8q (low cost) but if p95 > 200ms switch to x-16fp; if capacity < 10% switch to hosted-fallback. You can set it in the routing policy UI.
[11:10] Anita: Great. that's useful.
[11:13] Maya: Quick pause - any blockers for pilot?
[11:16] Marcus: Need security docs and pricing ballpark.
[11:18] Sophie: Also we need to validate SSO and provisioning flow in staging.
[11:22] Maya: Cool. We'll send SOC2 + SSO notes and sample pricing. Liam will attach KMS doc. We'll set up a pilot kickoff when you share traffic profile.
[11:33] Anita: Sounds good.
[11:36] [11:36] Liam: I'll also share a short recorder with recommended batch and cache configs for your workloads - that usually shows immediate savings.
[11:45] Maya: OK let's recap next steps.
[11:48] Maya: Action items: Maya send pricing and example workbook; Liam send SOC2 + KMS + SSO docs + recommended configs; Lakeside to share traffic profile and we schedule a pilot. Any objections?
[12:02] Sophie: No objections.
[12:05] Anita: One more question - can rollouts be automatically rolled back on quality regressions (not just latency)?
[12:11] Liam: Yes, you can configure automatic rollback on custom metrics, including eval scores you upload.
[12:18] Marcus: Perfect.
[12:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.
[12:24] (call ends)
